rv.q: The design elements support Greene’s work beautifully.
The cast at Playwrights Horizons is tuned to each other like an orchestra, but in lesser hands, it's easy to see how the ripple could fall flat.

But, as with a lot of the intriguing notions floating around in the ripple… , such ideas are talked about more than dramatized, and Anderson’s labored poeticism prevents them from being as wrenching to us as they are to Janice.
But the play feels like two or three scenes are missing, and they might be the really good ones.
But in these pleasant, comparatively passive 90 minutes, it just stirs up a ripple.
A glorious kaleidoscope that you will not soon forget.
There's an undeniable power to her lyricism, and to the ways this production brings her ideas to the surface with theatrical originality.

cn.t: Critics praise Christina Anderson's poetic memory play for its lyrical exploration of a family's civil rights activism around segregated swimming pools, with water serving as a powerful metaphor throughout this moving, nonlinear narrative.

vr.q: a piece I'll be thinking about for quite some time
